subject.title: fix(agents): bound finished bash process session retention

question: Should finished bash-process output remain pollable until its configured TTL in all cases, or should OpenClaw accept the proposed 50-session and 2,000,000-character global budget that can evict completed records earlier?
rationale: Both choices are internally coherent, but the patch deliberately changes the observable lifetime of completed process poll/log data and only a runtime owner can set that product and compatibility contract.

options.title: Accept bounded early eviction
options.body: Merge the hard count and aggregate budgets, accepting that burst workloads can expire completed process records before TTL in exchange for bounded gateway heap growth.

options.title: Revise the retention contract
options.body: Adjust the budget policy or lifecycle behavior before merge if completed process output must remain pollable for the full TTL under all supported workloads.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded early eviction
recommendation.body: Merge the hard count and aggregate budgets, accepting that burst workloads can expire completed process records before TTL in exchange for bounded gateway heap growth.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent merged history in the same process-registry state model and are the strongest available adjacent runtime contact.
